findings.text: Snapshot query supports realtime, monotonic, monotonic raw, boottime and an aux range, capturing cycle count, hardware ids, change sequences, system time and raw time plus a validity flag under sequence consistency.

Snapshot is marked invalid on entry and stays invalid when timekeeping is suspended, the id is unknown, aux data is missing, or the selected keeper is invalid; it becomes valid only after a stable sequence read.
Raw clock shares the monotonic keeper path with a zero offset and then copies the raw result into the system field so consumers use one field uniformly.
Scaled correction helper leaves its output unchanged and reports overflow when the intermediate quotient or remainder scaled by the multiplier would exceed 64 bit range.

Historical crosststamp correction skips empty histories, interpolates from the nearer history end, scales raw delta by a cycle fraction, and either derives system correction from a frequency ratio on discontinuity or scales the system delta similarly.
Interval test accepts a timestamp between inclusive bounds and also accepts wraparound when start exceeds end if the value is beyond start or before end.

Base conversion accepts a matching current clock id directly, otherwise requires a matching registered base descriptor and applies rational scaling plus offset before retagging the id, failing on missing base or zero factors.

Reverse conversion subtracts base offset then applies inverse rational scaling, while nanosecond to cycle conversion rejects shifts that would overflow width before applying shift, subtract and divide.
Realtime to base clock translation rejects times before the current base, converts the delta to cycles added to the last cycle, then converts to the requested base under sequence retry.

Device system crosststamp invokes a caller callback to capture device time plus system counter, normalizes the counter to the current clocksource, snapshots bases under sequence consistency, and interpolates from interval start when the counter lies outside the current interval.

Interpolation path requires caller history containing the captured counter without an intervening clocksource change, and derives partial and total spans plus a discontinuity flag from set sequences before historical adjustment.
Base presence check reads the current clock base pointer once without sequence protection and reports whether its identity matches the query.

Early init sets up core and aux keeper data, reads persistent wall and boot offset, validates the persistent value, derives wall to mono offset, enables the default clocksource, initializes NTP, installs internals and publishes with a full update under lock.
Basic setup initializes per keeper lock and sequence count, assigns identity to live and shadow copies, and sets the validity flag.
Adjtimex result groups audit data with a timespec delta and a clock set flag.
Syscore wiring connects resume and suspend callbacks through an ops object and a syscore object registered during init.

Clocksource change checks module reference and enable outside the lock, then under core irqsave lock forwards shadow time, swaps internals and publishes a full update before refreshing aux clocks and releasing the old module.
Aux clocksource refresh iterates active aux ids, takes each aux irqsave lock, skips invalid shadows, forwards time and reinstalls internals from the core raw clock before full publish.
Pulse and sleep updates serialize on the core irqsave lock with shadow forward and full publish, while aux set uses aux locking and aux enable holds core while nesting aux.
Aux disable path acquires the aux irq lock as its first observed step; the remainder is outside this fragment.
Persistent and suspend flags control RTC skip decisions, and sleep injection clears the need flag under lock before notifying timers about the change.
Boot time getter returns the difference between realtime and boot offsets as a timespec.
Multigrain coarse and precise realtime getters sample coarse or seconds plus nanoseconds with offset under sequence retry, then clamp against a shared monotonic floor.

Precise multigrain path tries to advance the shared floor with compare exchange, uses the fresh sample on success and adopts the winner value on contention, counting successful swaps in one build variant and doing nothing in the other.
Entropy fallback returns zero when suspended or without an installed clock, otherwise returns a direct clocksource read without sequence protection.
Auxiliary clock operations expose resolution query, timespec query, set and adjust through a common clock vector.

Aux set validates the new time and aux presence, forwards the shadow, refreshes base data, computes current monotonic time at the last cycle, stores the new offset as delta from now, then publishes a full update.
Aux resolution derives seconds and nanoseconds from a shared resolution helper, and aux timespec query maps success to zero and failure to a device error.

Aux enable assumes raw core conversion as initial frequency, clears shadow state, restores identity, installs the current raw clock, marks valid and publishes, leaving deviation to later user adjustment.
Snapshot and conversion readers use sequence begin and retry loops around keeper loads, with device crosststamp including the driver callback inside the retried region.
Persistent local clock marker is a global integer observed by time init paths.
Active aux set is tracked as a bitmask read once per refresh.
Aux keepers start invalid, become valid on enable, are skipped by readers and refresh while invalid, and are reinstalled from the core raw clock on clocksource change.
